newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin moves, plans relaxed week at country home.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin moves, plans relaxed week at country home.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin moved on Monday to the Rus country residence west of Moscow for the "final stage" of his rehabilitation after heart bypass surgery, the Kremlin said.
The president plans a relaxed week without any scheduled working meetings, his spokesman told Itar-Tass news agency.

The presidential press office said the Rus, 100 km (60 miles) from Moscow, had better facilities for the 65-year-old president's outdoor recreation than the Gorky-9 residence just outside the capital where he had moved last week.
"It has conditions allowing both the finalising of rehabilitation and work and active recreation," it said in a brief statement.
Interfax news agency said Yeltsin, who underwent a quintuple bypass operation on November 5, had been flown from Gorky-9 to Rus by helicopter.
"Apart from routine work the president ... is expected to make walks in the picturesque forests surrounding the residence," Interfax said.
Rus, earlier known as Zavidovo, has been a favourite hunting site for Soviet leaders, who often invited foreign dignitaries to shoot wild boars or ducks there.
It was not clear whether Yeltsin, also a devoted hunter, would be allowed to do any shooting.
Doctors said a visit to Rus before the operation worsened the president's heart condition and made things more difficult for those who prepared him for surgery.

Kremlin doctors say Yeltsin is now recovering well. Yegor Stroyev, chairman of the upper house of parliament, said after visiting Yeltsin last week that the president could make a trial visit to his Kremlin office by December 25.
Yeltsin does not plan to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin until after his return to the Kremlin, Tass quoted presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying.
The Kremlin has said Yeltsin will meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at Rus on January 4.
Yeltsin has also invited French President Jacques Chirac to visit him in early January. It has not been announced where they will meet.
Yeltsin is also planning to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in March. The venue is expected to be the United States.
